The patchbay device document: every input device the OS reports, joined

put.description:
The active profile decides how many channels the card's devices expose,
so this is how an interface with more inputs than the current profile
shows gets the rest of them. The switch renames, resizes and remaps the
card's devices, so the whole document is re-enumerated and returned —
callers must replace their copy rather than patch it.

The patchbay Refresh button: re-enumerate, re-run name reconciliation,

document. Also what the modal calls on open — plug and see.

Every synthesiser ships one of these because a lost note-off is a note
that hangs until something makes it stop.

The manual belt, exactly like the patchbay's Refresh: nothing retries in

The move a drum kit needs before anyone plays: one named, patched strip
per piece, ready to pan and fade. Only missing channels are added, so
pressing it twice costs nothing and existing levels survive.

The cheap half of "why is this silent?": it bisects a dead keyboard from

post.summary: Take a SoundFont into the library.
post.description:
The body is the file. Deliberately not multipart: the payload is one
opaque blob, multipart would add a dependency and a parser to say so,
and the name already has a home in the path.

Note that axum's `DefaultBodyLimit` does NOT apply to a body consumed as
a stream, so there is no limit to raise — and equally no limit at all
unless the handler enforces one. On a daemon with no authentication that
is not acceptable, so the byte budget is counted here, and exceeding it
aborts and unlinks rather than filling the disk.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: File name, slugged by the daemon

422.description: Not a SoundFont, or it would not load

delete.summary: Remove a soundfont from the library.
delete.description:
Only the internal library: a file on somebody's USB stick is theirs, and
the console says so rather than offering a button that deletes it.

409.description: An instrument is using it, or tape is rolling

get.summary: The one REST snapshot: everything a client needs to render the console.

Finished takes, newest first. Read fresh from disk on every call — the
manifest files are the source of truth and the list is short.

delete.summary: Permanently remove one take — audio, peaks and manifest together.
delete.description:
Refused while recording, and refused for the take being played: the
feeder threads hold open readers and reopen the files on every loop
pass, so unlinking underneath them would run playback off unlinked
inodes until a later wrap died somewhere confusing.

200.description: Deleted; the remaining takes, newest first

409.description: Recording, or that take is playing

get.summary: Waveform peaks for every track of a take, in `TakeDto.tracks` order.
get.description:
Binary layout (little-endian): `"TPKS"` · `version: u8 = 1` · `pad: u8`
· `track_count: u16` · `samples_per_bin: u32` · then per track:
`bin_count: u32` + `bin_count × (min: i16, max: i16)`.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Lane index within the latest take's tracks

200.description: Playhead moved (rebuilds the session while playing)

put.summary: Point the transport at a take of the open session.
put.description:
A property of the transport, so PUT with a body — the same shape as
`PUT /transport/loop` and `/monitor`, not a verb path like
`record/start`. Selecting is what makes `lanes`, `total_frames` and the
waveform describe that take, which is why it is separate from PLAY: the
point is to be able to LOOK at a take.

404.description: No such take in the open session

AudioLayer.description: Which device layer owns the audio hardware.

AudioStatusDto.description: The audio backend's own state, apart from any device.

backend.description: The backend's own name for itself.

card.description: The card the exclusive layer holds, when it holds one.

error.description: Why it is not running, when it is not.

layer.description: Which device layer the daemon was configured to run.

running.description:
Whether it is making sound right now. The exclusive layer is
running only while its card is open; it keeps retrying while not.

started.description:
Whether the backend's thread came up at boot at all. False is a
daemon-level failure that only a restart changes.

BusKind.description:
What a bus feeds. Groups mix into the master; aux buses feed an FX unit.
The split is the v1 cycle-prevention stage rule: strips → groups → aux →
fx → master, never backwards.

BusState.description: A group or aux bus strip. Renders like a channel strip without gain/arm.

pan.description:
Constant-power pan of a group into the master. Ignored for aux buses
(their output feeds an FX unit input, which is mono-summed).

Channel.description: A subscribable stream. Doubles as the routing key inside the hub.

ChannelEq.description: The Folio-style 3-band strip EQ: LF shelf, swept mid peak, HF shelf.

oneOf.description:
Continuous control gestures (fader/knob drags) ride WS, not REST —
the one deliberate divergence from magma, justified by gesture rate.

can_format.description:
Whether this installation can format a drive. False on package
installs, which ship no privileged helper — the console shows the
control disabled with a reason rather than failing on tap.

drives.description:
Every candidate filesystem, usable first — never filtered down to
the usable ones. A drive that is plugged in but unusable rendering
as nothing is indistinguishable from an empty port, which is the
failure this endpoint exists to make impossible.

DeviceReport.description: One row of the patchbay device document.

active.description: The OS default input — what `device: null` patches feed from.

card.description: The card this device belongs to. A profile change names the CARD.

channel_map.description:
The source's channel positions ("aux0,aux1,…"). NOT decoration:
the capture opens in exactly these positions, because the server
routes by position name and will synthesise a surround map that
drops most of a pro-audio source's inputs otherwise.

channels.description:
What the device exposes RIGHT NOW — a property of the card's active
profile, not of the hardware. 0 = unknown (an absent device was
never enumerated this boot).

error.description:
Why capture isn't running, when the failure happened at open time
(post-open stream deaths land in the journal only).

label.description:
The friendly print the system sound menu shows, when the source
layer provides one.

muted.description:
The source layer muted this input. It still opens, still streams,
and every meter fed from it reads silence — so a dead meter has an
explanation here that exists nowhere else in the report.

overruns.description: Whole frames dropped because the engine wasn't draining fast enough.

patched.description: Some strip references it (directly, via the default, or via an alias).

profile.description: The card's active profile, when it has one.

profiles.description:
Profiles this device's card can be switched into. More than one
means the channel count above is a choice, not a hardware limit.

reconciled_from.description:
The stored project name this device was matched from, when name
reconciliation adopted it under a changed name.

volume_percent.description:
The quietest channel's volume as a percentage of unity, when the
source layer says. None = unknown (raw ALSA, or an absent device),
which is deliberately distinct from 0.

device.description: The block device, when one backs this filesystem.

disk.description:
The whole disk this lives on, so the console can group partitions
under the drive they came from.

mount_point.description:
`null` when the drive is present but nothing mounted it — the case
that used to render as no drive at all.

reason.description: Why this is not a usable destination; `null` when it is.

DriveState.description:
Why a drive is or is not a usable destination.

Evaluated top-down, and the order is the point: these overlap (a
root-owned partition on the boot disk is both `System` and
`NotWritable`), so the winner is the reason the user can do least
about. "It is the boot disk" ends the conversation; "it is not
writable" invites a reformat.

EqBand.description:
One EQ band of a strip. `kind` is fixed per slot (low/mid/high); freq is
only user-swept on the mid band, but carrying it uniformly keeps the DSP
coefficient path shape-free.

FaderTarget.description:
Which fader a level command addresses; doubles as the mute/PFL/rename
target (the master supports only fader moves in v1 — see `apply`).

device.description:
The whole disk, as `DriveDto.disk` names it ("/dev/sda"). A
partition is refused: formatting one strands the rest of the drive.

label.description: The exFAT volume label, which becomes the drive's printed name.

feedback.description: 0.0 .. 0.95; capped below unity so the loop always decays.

FxParams.description:
Parameters of a built-in effect. The serde tag doubles as the effect kind
on the wire, so `FxState` never carries a separate `kind` field to drift.

FxState.description:
A built-in effect unit: fed by one aux bus, returned into the master at
`return_level_db`.

InputAssign.description:
What feeds a strip: a hardware input (a device by OS name, plus a
channel within it) or one side of a virtual instrument.

`Device { device: None }` means the system default input — the shape
every pre-multi-device manifest carries.

The wire form is **untagged**, and that is deliberate: a device patch
serializes to exactly the bytes it always has, so a manifest written by
this daemon still opens under an older one. Only instrument patches —
which an older daemon could not render anyway — carry a shape it has
never seen. Instruments live in their own channel space rather than
borrowing a reserved device name, so device identity, its rename
reconciliation and its slot allocator never learn they exist.

InputAssignBody.description:
What to patch a strip to: either a device (by OS name, `null` = the
system default input) or a virtual instrument, plus a channel within it.

`channel` is shared by both because it means the same thing either way,
and naming both `device` and `instrument` is refused rather than
silently resolved — a patch that quietly picks the wrong source reads as
a silent strip with no explanation.

InstrumentId.description:
A virtual instrument in the rack. Never reused within a session:
it is the printed slot ("INST 3"), the patch identity a strip
holds, and the seed for the link tape's colour.

InstrumentPatch.description:
Any subset of an instrument's settings. Absent fields stay put.

The daemon fans this out into the two commands the reducer draws a line
between — voice settings rebuild the synth and are refused while the
tape rolls, performance settings do not and are not.

presets.description:
Presets the loaded soundfont carries, so the console can say
whether a preset number means anything.

reason.description:
The daemon's own sentence for why, in the console's voice. `None`
when there is nothing to explain.

resident_bytes.description: Resident sample data, so a Pi's memory budget is legible.

InstrumentSplit.description:
One mixer channel of a split instrument: a named slice of the keyboard.

This is how a drum kit reaches the desk as separate faders. A SoundFont
kit is one MIDI channel with a different drum on every key, so the only
axis that separates a kick from a snare is the key number.

A split is **mono**, deliberately. A drum is a point source you pan
yourself, and the alternative — two strips per piece — turns a five-piece
kit into ten channels of desk to manage before anyone has played a note.
An unsplit instrument stays stereo, because a piano's stereo image is
the thing you actually want.

ranges.description:
Inclusive key ranges this channel answers to.

A list, not one range, because the General MIDI drum map
**interleaves** toms and hi-hats — 41 tom, 42 hat, 43 tom, 44 hat,
45 tom, 46 hat. A single contiguous range cannot put the toms on
one fader and the hats on another, which is the first thing anyone
mixing drums wants.

InstrumentState.description:
A virtual instrument: a SoundFont, a preset within it, and the MIDI
traffic it answers to.

Part of the console document, so it persists in `project.toml` and
reaches every client through the mixer snapshot. Note what is *not*
here: whether the soundfont actually loaded, how many presets it has,
whether its port is connected. Those are facts about the machine, not
about the desk, and they travel on the instruments report the way a
device's status travels on the devices report — the same rule that keeps
the transport out of the reducer.

effects.description:
`rustysynth`'s own reverb and chorus. Off by default: the console
already ships an FX 1 reverb send, and stacking a second one costs a
Pi real CPU to sound worse.

midi_channel.description: `None` = omni: every channel on that port.

port.description: MIDI source port, by name. `None` = bound to nothing.

soundfont.description:
A file name within the soundfont library — never a path.
`project.toml` travels to a USB stick and opens on another box, so a
path would be a promise about a machine the session may never see
again. `None` = nothing chosen yet, which is silence with a reason.

splits.description:
Per-drum (or per-region) mixer channels. Empty = one stereo output,
which is what a piano wants; non-empty = one mono channel per split,
which is what a kit wants.

InstrumentStatus.description:
Why an instrument is or is not making sound.

This is machinery, not document — the same split that keeps the
transport out of the reducer. It lives on the instruments report
alongside a sentence, because "the strip is silent" must always have an
answer somewhere in the console.

InstrumentsDto.description:
Everything the Instruments tab needs in one read: what the console
holds, why each one is or is not sounding, what MIDI is available, and
what there is to load.

One document rather than three endpoints because the three answers are
entangled — deleting a soundfont changes an instrument's status, and
unplugging a keyboard changes its reason. Split reads would let the
console render a pair that never existed together.

instruments.description: The console document's instruments, in rack order.

max_upload_bytes.description:
Ceiling on an upload, so the console can refuse a file before
spending twenty minutes sending it.

reports.description: Machine truth about each one, keyed by the same id.

soundfont_dir.description: Where uploads land, for the console to print.

LaneDto.description:
Playback gate for one lane of the latest take (index-aligned with the
take's tracks).

MasterState.description: The master output section: one stereo fader and its own record arm.

MeterDto.description: One metered point in a `meters` batch.

MeterKey.description: What a metered point on the console refers to.

MidiDto.description:
The MIDI patch bay in one read: routes, their state, and both
directions' ports.

take_tracks.description:
Sidecar names the selected take carries, for the take-playback
picker. A route names one of these rather than a take number,
because a take number does not survive the next take.

MidiOutPortReport.description: One MIDI output port, joined with what the daemon knows about it.

absent.description: A route names it but the system does not offer it.

errors.description:
Writes the port refused. An interface that went away mid-song shows
up here before it shows up as absent.

id.description: The port's NAME — stable across a replug, unlike its client number.

routes.description:
Routes feeding it. More than one is a merge, which is legal here
and worth drawing.

sent.description:
Messages sent since it opened.

The only thing that distinguishes "wired and nobody is playing"
from "wired wrong" — an output port has no meter, so without a
counter a dead cable and a quiet keyboard look identical.

absent.description: An instrument references it but the system does not offer it.

connected.description: True when an instrument is bound to it and it is connected.

id.description:
Stable across a replug: the port's name, not its ALSA client
number, which the kernel hands out afresh every time.

channel.description:
`None` = pass the source's own channel through. `Some(n)` = force
every message onto channel n, which is what a module listening on
one channel needs.

port.description:
The output port by the name the sequencer prints, e.g.
`"Juno-6:Juno-6 MIDI 1 24:0"`.

Known limitation, shared with `InstrumentState::port` and verified
against a live ALSA sequencer: **that name embeds the client
number**, which the kernel hands out afresh on every replug — so a
route stored today can name a port that will not exist after the
synth is unplugged and plugged back in. It fails visibly (the port
reports `absent` and the console says it is not connected) rather
than silently sending to the wrong device, because the new name
matches nothing. Fixing it means matching on the client-number-free
prefix on BOTH sides at once; doing it on one side only would let an
instrument and a route disagree about what a port is called.

source.description: Declared last so the emitted TOML reads scalars-then-table.

MidiRouteReport.description: One route, joined with what the daemon knows about it.

reason.description: The daemon's own sentence. `None` when there is nothing to explain.

MidiRouteRequest.description: A change to one MIDI route.

MidiRouteStatus.description: Why one route is or is not carrying anything.

oneOf.description:
Echo a rack instrument: everything it receives goes out too, so an
external synth plays the same part the SoundFont does.

Forward a MIDI INPUT port. Several routes may name one output —
that is the merge, and it is the one place the patch bay's
"one feed per output" rule does not apply, because MIDI events
interleave where audio would have to be summed.

Stream a take's `.mid` sidecar back out while it plays.

Named rather than numbered: the take number is *transport* state,
and a route stored in `project.toml` has to name something that
survives the next take. The sidecar's name is the only such handle,
and it is already on the wire as `TakeMidiTrackDto.name`.

MidiSource.description:
What is sent to a MIDI output port.

A separate array from [`OutputPatch`] rather than one enum with both,
because the two share no field but "a name of a thing to send to" — and
that name means an ALSA *PCM device* in one and an ALSA *sequencer
port* in the other. Folding them together is the two-shapes-in-one-type
failure `InputAssign`'s hand-written `Deserialize` exists to prevent.

Transport sync (MIDI clock, MTC) is deliberately absent: this project
has no tempo, no bar and no beat, so a clock it emitted would be a
claim it cannot support.

oneOf.description:
Upsert one aux send. A level at the floor is simply silent — the
send always exists toward every aux bus.
Where the strip's main signal goes (master or a group bus).

Arm a strip (its own dry track) or the master (the mix) for the
next take. Arming mid-take changes the NEXT take, not the running one.
The "Arm All" button: every loaded strip at once (master untouched).

Everything `rustysynth` can only take at construction. Rebuilding a
synth means reloading its samples, so this is a topology change and
the tape refuses it — mid-take is exactly when you cannot afford a
pause to read a soundfont off a USB stick.

Everything a running synth accepts: the preset, what it listens to,
and its name. Deliberately NOT frozen while recording — changing
sound mid-take is normal playing, and a keyboardist who finds
themselves on the wrong MIDI channel has to be able to fix it.

How an instrument reaches the desk: one stereo pair, or a fader per
named piece. Rebuilds the synth, so it is a topology change.

Put every one of an instrument's channels on the desk in one move.

The setup step a kit needs before anyone plays: six drums, six
faders, named and patched, ready to pan. Adds only what is missing,
so pressing it twice is safe and pressing it after adding a split
does the obvious thing rather than doubling the desk.

Patch one output channel — an upsert keyed on the JACK, because the
jack is the identity. A jack holds at most one patch, so re-patching
replaces what was there rather than stacking a second feed onto it;
one SOURCE may feed many jacks, the exact mirror of one jack feeding
many strips on the way in.
Unpatch one output channel, named by the jack.

Move a patch's tap and nothing else.

Its own command so a console that PUTs its whole form does not stop
the tape to flip a switch — the same split `patch_commands` already
makes between an instrument's voice and its performance.

Upsert one MIDI route. Keyed on (port, source), so pressing the
same button twice is one route — the `AddInstrumentStrips` idiom.
Several DIFFERENT sources may name one port; that is the merge.
Remove one MIDI route by the same key.

MixCommand.description:
A mutation of the mixer document. The API-facing command enum: REST
handlers and the WS `set` op both reduce to this.

MixerState.description:
The whole console document: the single authoritative mix state the daemon
owns, the UI mirrors, and the project manifest persists.

instruments.description:
Declared after the other arrays and before `master` on purpose:
`toml` serializes in declaration order and refuses a value after a
table, so a scalar section between the arrays-of-tables would make
every manifest unwritable.

midi_routes.description:
MIDI routes: instrument echo, thru/merge, and take playback. Same
position rule as its neighbours above.

outputs.description:
The output patch bay. Same reason for the position as `instruments`
above, and `default` for the same reason: a manifest written before
outputs existed carries no key at all.

MonitorTarget.description:
Where the playback mix goes: the console's hardware output, or the
browser monitor stream (M6). Hardware until the stream lands.

seed.description: What the new session's desk starts from.

OutputDeviceReport.description:
One row of the output patch bay device document. The mirror of
[`DeviceReport`], carrying the same honest-failure fields for the same
reasons — read the other way round.

channels.description:
What the device exposes RIGHT NOW. 0 = unknown (absent, never
enumerated this boot).

monitor_channels.description:
How many of `channels` the monitor has taken and the patch bay may
not offer.

muted.description:
The sink layer muted this output. It still opens, still streams,
and the room hears nothing — and an output has no meter to show it,
so this field is the only place a dead PA is explainable.

worst_block_us.description:
Worst engine block this second, in microseconds. 0 where the
backend does not measure it.

xruns.description:
ALSA xruns recovered on this device. Always 0 off the real-time
backend, which is the only one that opens a `hw:` PCM.

OutputJack.description:
A physical output channel — the identity of a patch.

One jack, at most one patch: the mirror of one strip, at most one
input. An output carries one signal, and summing two sources onto it
would make this a mixer rather than a patch bay.

device.description:
`None` = the system default output — the meaning
`InputAssign::Device { device: None }` already has on the way in.

oneOf.description:
One stereo pair — a piano, a pad, anything whose stereo image is
the point.

The General MIDI drum map as named faders: Kick, Snare, Toms,
HiHat, Cymbals, Percussion.
Whatever splits the caller names.

OutputLayout.description: How an instrument reaches the desk.

OutputPatch.description: One direct out: a point in the console wired to a jack.

source.description:
Declared last so the emitted TOML reads scalars-then-table, the
shape every other record in the manifest already has.

source_channel.description:
Channel within the source: 0 for a strip or an aux bus, 0 or 1 for
a group bus or the master.

tap.description:
Where the signal is tapped.

Pre-fader by default, which in this engine means post-gain,
post-EQ, **pre-mute and pre-fader** — the same point the meter and
record taps use. A direct out is for the monitor engineer, and a
front-of-house fader move must not change what they get.

OutputPatchReport.description: One patch, joined with what the daemon knows about where it goes.

reason.description:
The daemon's own sentence, in the console's voice. `None` when
there is nothing to explain.

OutputPatchRequest.description:
A change to one output channel.

A tagged envelope rather than a nullable field, because the identity
here is TWO values: a body naming a patch and saying `null` in the same
breath would be representable, and would have to be refused at runtime.

OutputPatchStatus.description: Why one patch is or is not carrying signal.

OutputSource.description:
What feeds an output channel.

The same three cases as [`crate::FaderTarget`] and [`crate::MeterKey`],
and a third type on purpose: those name what a level command moves and
what a peak describes. This names what leaves the box. They agree
today; nothing makes them agree tomorrow — and calling this one
"fader target" would put the word fader into the wire shape of a tap
that is deliberately pre-fader.

OutputsDto.description:
The whole output patch bay in one read — the document half and the
machine half together.

One document for the reason `InstrumentsDto` is one document: pulling
an interface changes a patch's status, and split reads would let the
console render a pair that never existed together.

supported.description:
Whether this backend can drive patchable outputs at all. False
makes every mutation a 501 rather than a silent no-op.

ProfileReport.description: One profile a device's card can be switched into.

description.description: "Pro Audio" — what the system sound panel prints.

RealtimeDto.description: What the machine granted the audio thread.

reason.description: Why it is not better than this, in a sentence someone can act on.

RecordFormat.description:
What the take writer puts on disk. Bit depth folds into the variant so
illegal combinations (float FLAC) are unrepresentable.

active_sample_rate.description: What the engine graph runs at — immutable per boot.

configured_destination.description:
The persisted preference — differs from `destination` when the
configured drive was missing at boot and the daemon fell back.

configured_sample_rate.description: What the prefs ask for — takes effect at the next daemon start.

destination.description: The projects root the next take lands on.

project_name.description: The open project at the destination.

RouteTarget.description: Where a strip's main (post-fader, post-pan) signal goes.

SendState.description: One aux send from a strip toward a bus.

SendTap.description:
Where an aux send taps the strip signal. Pre-fader for monitor-style
sends, post-fader for FX (the classic default: FX level follows the mix).

oneOf.description:
The full document — sent on every Mixer subscribe (and structural
changes, from M3). Clients replace their mirror wholesale.
One applied mutation, broadcast to ALL clients (multi-UI sync).
Coalesced meter batch at the pump rate. Droppable.
Transport state changed (play/stop/record/seek/gates).

Playhead progress at the pump rate while playing. Droppable; frames
are take-timeline frames derived from real audio, not wall clock.

Freshly closed peak bins from the take writer — the live waveform.
`bins` is interleaved (min, max) pairs scaled by 32767.

The candidate drive list, pushed when the mount table changes and
once on subscribe. Carries only the drives — the active and default
destinations belong to the recording settings the client already
holds, and duplicating them here would give them two homes.

The open session's takes, newest first — pushed whenever the shelf
changes. Same mapping as `GET /api/v1/takes`, so a push and a poll
can never disagree.

The open session changed — created, opened or renamed. Carries only
the open one; a client showing the list refetches, and one showing
just the tape label never has to.

id.description:
The directory name. Stable across a rename — renaming retitles the
manifest and never moves the directory, so an id a client is
holding stays valid.

open.description: Exactly one session in a list is open.

SessionSeed.description:
What a new session's desk starts from, ordered by how much of the
current rig it keeps.

root.description: The projects root these live under — the active destination.

root_present.description:
False when the destination has gone away (drive unplugged). An
empty list then means "we cannot see them", not "there are none" —
two different sentences the console must not merge.

sessions.description: Newest first, in the same order an adopt would pick from.

SetCardProfile.description: Which profile to put a sound card into.

card.description:
The card, as `DeviceReport.card` names it. Profiles belong to the
card, not to any one of its devices.

id.description: Library id — the file name, which is also what an instrument stores.

volume.description:
Volume label for a removable file, so the console can say *which*
stick it wants back.

SoundfontOrigin.description: Where a file came from. Drives what the console offers to do with it.

unpatched_outputs.description:
The jacks that went quiet with it. A structural change, so a
snapshot follows — but the console wants to say what it just
did, and "removing Ch 3 also unpatched OUT 5" is that sentence.

oneOf.description:
Carries the strips it unpatched, so a client's mirror does not need
to re-derive which channels just went quiet.

unrouted_ports.description: The MIDI output ports that stopped echoing it.

oneOf.description:
Both instrument edits report the whole instrument rather than the
fields that moved: it is small, and a client that misses one field
of a preset change would render a lie about what is playing.

The strips "add all channels" created. A structural change, so the
daemon broadcasts a snapshot too; the delta carries the list because
the console wants to say what it just did.

The whole patch, not the fields that moved: a client keys outputs by
jack, and a half-patch would leave it drawing a jack whose source it
cannot name.

StateDelta.description:
What a successful `apply` changed — the WS `state_changed` payload.
Semantically complete per change: a client patches its mirror from the
delta alone. Structural changes broadcast a full snapshot instead.

StripPatch.description:
Any subset of a strip's controls. Absent fields stay put; `input` is
double-optional so `null` explicitly unpatches while absence means
"leave it".

StripState.description:
One channel strip, top to bottom like the panel: input, gain, EQ, sends,
pan, fader, switches.

midi_tracks.description:
MIDI sidecars beside the audio, one per instrument that was armed.
Empty for every take without one, which is most of them.

strip_id.description:
The strip this track tapped — absent for the master mix and for
takes cut before the field existed.

TransportDto.description:
Transport state, pushed on the Transport channel on every state change
and served over REST. Position ticks ride `PlaybackPosition` instead.

engine_sample_rate.description:
What the engine graph runs at — immutable per boot. A take cut at
another rate can be selected and read, but not played: there is no
resampler, so PLAY refuses. Carried here so the console can disable
PLAY and print why rather than discovering it via a 422.

lanes.description:
Playback gates for the SELECTED take, index-aligned with its
tracks. Empty while recording — there is no playback set to gate.

latest_take.description:
The newest finished take on the shelf. Equals `take` unless the
console is reviewing an older one. `null` on an empty session.

sample_rate.description: The SELECTED take's rate; the engine's own while recording.

take.description:
The selected take — what PLAY would roll. While recording, the take
being written.

total_frames.description:
Length of the selected take (its longest track); 0 while recording,
where the client uses its own live frame count instead.

destination.description: Absolute path of the new destination. Omitted = leave alone.

WsAck.description:
Tags a `state_changed` broadcast with the client gesture that caused it,
so the issuing tab can reconcile its optimistic value.
